cards.body:
Luna, a 6-year-old corgi, is back with her owner Molly Wing-Berman after going missing when an EF0 tornado struck the Bay St. Lucie community in Port St. Lucie. The tornado pushed open Wing-Berman's front door, made a large hole in the wall, swept mail and items from surfaces out through the back door, and deposited debris in the pool.

Wing-Berman had taken her 2-year-old rescue dog Enzo to the laundry room for safety as the tornado approached. She tried to bring Luna along, but when the corgi did not respond or follow, Wing-Berman thought she was hiding under the bed. Wing-Berman and her daughter searched the house and yard after the storm passed.

Neighbors eventually found Luna three streets away. Wing-Berman said the dog was shaking and has stayed close to her since returning home. Luna now has a new nickname: Luna ToTo. It remains unclear whether Luna was picked up by the tornado or ran out after being spooked by the storm.

hero.body:
The Fort Pierce City Commission voted 3-2 this week to appoint Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney while conducting a nationwide search for a permanent replacement. The transition follows the commission's decision not to renew City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract, Assistant City Attorney Felicia Holloman's resignation, and the departure of temporary attorney Caroline Valentin at the end of August.

Commissioner Michael Broderick voted against Wallace's appointment and expressed concern about the timing of the legal department changes. Broderick said several significant development projects are expected to come before the City Commission soon, including potential changes to the South Beach Overlay on South Hutchinson Island. The South Beach Overlay currently limits building heights and density, and Broderick said removing those restrictions could allow much taller development on the island.

Broderick questioned the decision to appoint Wallace, who previously worked in the City Attorney's Office before becoming deputy city manager. He said appointing the assistant city manager to serve as a charter officer creates a conflict with multiple reporting lines. Supporters of the appointment said Wallace's legal background and familiarity with city operations provide continuity while the city loses much of its legal staff.

The City Commission approved a contract with executive search firm S. Rene Narloch & Associates to recruit a permanent city attorney. The agreement authorizes up to nearly $31,000 in fees and expenses for the search process. City officials expect Wallace's interim appointment to return to the commission in the form of a formal contract and resolution in the coming months.
hero.headline: Fort Pierce City Commission shakeup leaves legal department without permanent leadership as development decisions loom

hero.body:
Fort Pierce's City Commission voted 3-2 this week to appoint Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney after City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract was not renewed, Assistant City Attorney Felicia Holloman resigned, and temporary attorney Caroline Valentin is set to leave at the end of the month. The sudden loss of all three legal staff members comes as the city faces high-profile development decisions on South Hutchinson Island, including potential changes to the South Beach Overlay that currently limits building heights and density. Commissioner Michael Broderick voted against the appointment and said the city now lacks independent legal representation to guide commissioners through the volatile projects.

Broderick told CBS12 News the timing concerns him because several significant development proposals are slated to come before the City Commission in short order. He said removing South Beach Overlay restrictions could clear the way for much taller development on South Hutchinson Island. Broderick said appointing Wallace creates a conflict because she will serve as both a charter officer and deputy city manager. "In my opinion, that reeks of duplicity and multiple bosses you need to report to," Broderick said. "I'm not sure how that is even possible to do."

Supporters of Wallace's appointment said her previous experience working in the City Attorney's Office before becoming deputy city manager positions her to maintain continuity while the city loses much of its legal staff. They said her legal background and familiarity with city operations will help keep city business moving during a nationwide search for a permanent city attorney. City officials expect the interim appointment to return to the commission in the form of a formal contract and resolution.

The commission approved a contract with executive search firm S. Renée Narloch & Associates to recruit a permanent city attorney. The agreement authorizes up to nearly $31,000 in fees and expenses for the search process. The search is expected to continue over the coming months.

Luna, a 6-year-old corgi, is back with her owner Molly Wing-Berman after going missing when an EF0 tornado struck the Bay St. Lucie community in Port St. Lucie. The tornado pushed open Wing-Berman's front door, made a large hole in the wall, swept mail and items from surfaces out through the back door, and deposited debris in the pool.

Wing-Berman had taken her 2-year-old rescue dog Enzo to the laundry room for safety as the tornado approached. She tried to bring Luna along, but when the corgi did not respond or follow, Wing-Berman thought she was hiding under the bed. Wing-Berman and her daughter searched the house and yard after the storm passed.

Neighbors eventually found Luna three streets away. Wing-Berman said the dog was shaking and has stayed close to her since returning home. Luna now has a new nickname: Luna ToTo. It remains unclear whether Luna was picked up by the tornado or ran out after being spooked by the storm.
cards.headline: Luna the corgi reunited with owner after EF0 tornado in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: A 6-year-old corgi that went missing when an EF0 tornado struck the Bay St. Lucie community in Port St. Lucie has been returned to her owner. Neighbors found Luna three streets away from her home after the storm pushed open the front door.

hero.body:
Fort Pierce's City Commission voted 3-2 this week to appoint Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney after City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract was not renewed, Assistant City Attorney Felicia Holloman resigned, and temporary attorney Caroline Valentin is set to leave at the end of the month. The sudden loss of all three legal staff members comes as the city faces high-profile development decisions on South Hutchinson Island, including potential changes to the South Beach Overlay that currently limits building heights and density. Commissioner Michael Broderick voted against the appointment and said the city now lacks independent legal representation to guide commissioners through the volatile projects.

Broderick told CBS12 News the timing concerns him because several significant development proposals are slated to come before the City Commission in short order. He said removing South Beach Overlay restrictions could clear the way for much taller development on South Hutchinson Island. Broderick said appointing Wallace creates a conflict because she will serve as both a charter officer and deputy city manager. "In my opinion, that reeks of duplicity and multiple bosses you need to report to," Broderick said. "I'm not sure how that is even possible to do."

Supporters of Wallace's appointment said her previous experience working in the City Attorney's Office before becoming deputy city manager positions her to maintain continuity while the city loses much of its legal staff. They said her legal background and familiarity with city operations will help keep city business moving during a nationwide search for a permanent city attorney. City officials expect the interim appointment to return to the commission in the form of a formal contract and resolution.

The commission approved a contract with executive search firm S. Renée Narloch & Associates to recruit a permanent city attorney. The agreement authorizes up to nearly $31,000 in fees and expenses for the search process. The search is expected to continue over the coming months.
hero.headline: Fort Pierce loses three legal staff as commission appoints deputy city manager interim attorney ahead of South Hutchinson Island development votes
